turns.originalText: ## Prompt for Content Handler Module Create a content handler module for a Chrome extension that manages content script injection across tabs. This should be a "core module" that other modules can use to inject their content scripts. Context: This is part of a modular Chrome extension system where each module is a single file Modules follow a specific pattern with manifest, exported functions, and tests The extension uses a state management system where modules communicate through shared state Follow the coding style: extracted single-purpose functions, early returns, descriptive names, minimal inline logic Requirements: Module Structure: Single file: `content-handler.module.js` Export manifest with name, version, permissions, actions, state reads/writes Follow the module pattern from this example structure: Core Functionality: `register(moduleName, contentFunction, options)` - Register a module's content script `inject(moduleName)` - Manually inject a registered module's content Track what's injected where in state Tab Lifecycle Management: Auto-inject 'all' pattern scripts into new tabs Handle tab navigation (re-inject if needed) Clean up state when tabs close Skip chrome://, chrome-extension:// and other restricted URLs State Structure: Important Patterns to Follow: Each module's content script is injected separately (not aggregated) Use chrome.scripting.executeScript with func parameter Handle errors gracefully (some tabs can't be injected) Module initialization should set up tab listeners Tests to Include: Test registration with different patterns Test injection into valid/invalid tabs Test tab lifecycle handling Test state management Style Example from Codebase: Create this module following these patterns and conventions. Make it production-ready with proper error handling and tests.
